# Run Log

> A free, open-source run explorer. Drop in a FIT or GPX file from a running
> watch and read what actually happened during the run — what changed, where it
> changed, and what might account for it. The file is parsed in the browser and
> is never uploaded unless the runner deliberately shares a run, in which case
> it is encrypted first. There is no account.

This file follows the llms.txt convention, which is a proposal rather than a
standard: no assistant is known to require it, and nothing here is a substitute
for the page itself saying what it is. It costs one static file, and it is the
one place a summary of the site can be written for a reader that fetches HTML
and does not run JavaScript.

## What the site is

Run Log is a single client-rendered page at https://runlogapp.com/. There is no
route to crawl beyond the root. A run exists only in the reader's own browser
for as long as the tab is open, so there is no public per-run URL to index.

Shared runs live under /s/, and that path is disallowed in robots.txt and served
with `noindex`. A share link is unguessable and its payload is encrypted with a
key held in the link's fragment, which is never sent to the server — so there is
nothing there to crawl, and nothing a crawler could read if it did.

## What it does

- Reads FIT and GPX files from running watches, in the browser.
- Resamples the run onto a uniform one-second grid, then builds a page of cards
  from it: pace, heart rate and its zones, cadence, power, elevation and
  gradient, kilometre splits, stops and walking, best sections.
- Adjusts pace for gradient using the Minetti cost-of-running curve, so a
  kilometre run uphill can be compared with one run on the flat.
- Lets the runner add what the watch could not record — a gel, a drink, a
  cramp, a blood lactate reading — and reads the run around those marks.
- States a confidence and a provenance for every claim, and declines to make a
  claim the file cannot support rather than filling the gap.

## What it is not

- Not a training log, a race diary or a social network. It reads one run at a
  time and explains it.
- Not medical, coaching or training advice. Every figure comes from a consumer
  device and can be wrong.
- Not a service. Nothing is uploaded, so there is nothing to sign in to.
